turns.assessment: The only observed change is an abrupt pre-FEC BER increase at the S23 receiver. Its received power, estimated OSNR, DGD, and SOP rate remained stable, while all monitored amplifiers and channel monitors on the incoming path also remained stable. This strongly localizes the penalty to trx.och143.z rather than to line power, noise, polarization, or span degradation; a channel-specific WSS filter penalty remains a smaller alternative because it can reduce quality without changing power.

proposals.rationale: Receiver-local degradation directly explains increased BER at S23 with normal optical-path metrics and no corresponding change at the S24 interface.

A shifted or narrowed WSS passband can produce a channel quality penalty while leaving received power and ordinary OCM OSNR measurements unchanged, but the evidence does not identify a particular WSS.
Margin erosion can raise BER with otherwise normal measurements, but it is described as a slow decline and is less consistent with the observed level change near t=606 s.
